**The mechanism (MVCC, from `mdb.c`):**

**What a reader records.** Each reader thread owns one slot in the shared reader table — an `MDB_reader` (union around `MDB_rxbody`) containing its process id (`mr_pid`), thread id (`mr_tid`, used only for stale-reader detection), and the field that matters: its current transaction id (`mr_txnid`; 0 = no open read transaction).

**Where.** The slots are the `mti_readers[]` array of `MDB_txninfo`, the lock table in the shared-memory start of the lock file (`env->me_txns`). Its header (`MDB_txbody`) also carries the last committed transaction id (`mti_txnid`, newer mdb.master: `mtis_latest_txnid` — the writer publishes it at commit) and `mti_numreaders`, the high-water count of used slots (default max 126, `mdb_env_set_maxreaders`).

**The lock-free part.** On its first read txn a thread locks the reader mutex (`env->me_rmutex` / `mti_rmutex`) just long enough to claim a free slot (`mr_pid == 0`, index < `mti_numreaders`, which it bumps); the slot number is remembered in thread-local storage (`mdb_tls`), so the thread reuses it forever after. Every subsequent txn begin is just `mr_txnid = mti_txnid`, and txn end clears `mr_txnid = 0` — both with no lock: each thread writes only its own slot, and the txnid is one aligned word, so stores are atomic and the writer reading a stale value is merely conservative. Snapshot isolation comes from the mmap: old page versions stay untouched until reclaimed.

**When a mutex is actually needed.** `mti_rmutex`: only for slot registration/allocation and stale-reader cleanup (`mdb_reader_check` clears slots whose `mr_pid`/`mr_tid` is dead). `mti_wmutex`: the single-writer mutex, held for the entire write transaction. Neither is ever held while a read transaction is open.

**Why the writer isn't blocked.** At commit the writer scans the table (`mdb_find_oldest`) for the oldest live `mr_txnid` and reuses only pages freed at or before it; pages freed since are kept as per-txnid entries in the `FREE` sub-database until every reader has moved past. Readers delay *space reclamation*, never the writer.

ANSWER: Each reader thread owns one `MDB_reader` slot in the shared lock table `MDB_txninfo.mti_readers[]` (`env->me_txns`) and records its current transaction id in `mr_txnid` (plus identity: `mr_pid`, `mr_tid` for stale-reader cleanup); the slot is claimed once under the reader mutex `mti_rmutex` (remembered via TLS) and thereafter updated lock-free — `mr_txnid = mti_txnid` (a.k.a. `mtis_latest_txnid`) on begin, cleared to 0 on end — because each thread writes only its own single-word-aligned field; the writer holds `mti_wmutex` for a whole write txn and at commit computes the oldest live `mr_txnid` via `mdb_find_oldest` to defer reuse of pages freed since that point, so mutexes are needed only for slot allocation/cleanup and writer serialization — never during an open read transaction.
